1. Risk cap can be exceeded by parallel takes 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>marketLoop reads assetInv through assetExposure and ExposureAllows before enqueuing an
>intent on the shared executor, but aggregate exposure is incremented only after PlaceTracked
>returns and its fills are recorded. When two live-market goroutines check the same asset before
>either receipt is processed, both can approve against the same stale value and their sequentially
>executed fills can collectively exceed MaxAssetExposure.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[core/internal/maker/engine.go[391]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/6/files#diff-5fa2c2f0354a49f1be3c74a5784df117c6be458f3be5b711bf5103878f93622fR391-R391) > >```diff >+ if ok, prospective := ExposureAllows(e.assetExposure(im.Asset), delta, e.Params.MaxAssetExposure); !ok { >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Unsynchronized check-then-record logic can violate the newly introduced aggregate exposure cap.
>
> > [PR-#2](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/2) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Each live market runs in a separate goroutine and performs the exposure read and cap check before
>placing its intent on the shared queue. Although execute later serializes transaction writes,
>record increments aggregate exposure only after the transaction completes and the returned receipt
>fills are decoded, leaving a window in which another market loop can observe and approve against the
>old exposure.
>

2. Resting quotes bypass the asset cap 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>ExposureAllows runs only in the immediate-take branch, while the maker branch submits post-only
>Buy Up and Buy Down orders using only per-market MaxInventory checks and without reserving or
>checking aggregate asset exposure. When same-direction resting orders fill asynchronously across
>multiple live windows—including through reconciliation—while opposing quotes remain unfilled, their
>combined inventory can pass MaxAssetExposure without another guarded take occurring.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[core/internal/maker/engine.go[R391-397]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/6/files#diff-5fa2c2f0354a49f1be3c74a5784df117c6be458f3be5b711bf5103878f93622fR391-R397) > >```diff >+ if ok, prospective := ExposureAllows(e.assetExposure(im.Asset), delta, e.Params.MaxAssetExposure); !ok { >+ e.bump(func(s *Stats) { s.ExposureRefused++ }) >+ e.Log.Printf("[%s] t-%3.0fs fair=%.3f book=%.3f/%.3f TAKE REFUSED asset exposure cap"+ >+ " (%s would reach %.1f of %.1f across every live %s window, edge=%.3f)", >+ label, secsLeft, fair, bestBid, bestAsk, im.Asset, prospective, e.Params.MaxAssetExposure, im.Asset, tk.Edge) >+ continue >+ } >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Unprotected resting orders bypass the PR’s stated cross-window exposure-cap objective.
>
> > [PR-#2](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/2) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The cited take path places the new ExposureAllows guard only inside the tk.Any() branch, whereas
>the normal two-sided quote path submits both post-only orders without an asset-level check. Because
>these resting orders remain live and can later fill in counterparty transactions or through
>reconciliation, each market can stay within its individual inventory limit while fills across
>several windows collectively exceed the aggregate cap.
>

>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Ensure resting maker orders cannot create aggregate asset exposure beyond the configured cap. The current asset-level guard protects immediate takes only, while post-only orders across multiple windows can fill after submission and collectively exceed `MaxAssetExposure`. > >## Issue Context >Post-only orders are the primary maker path and remain live asynchronously, including through the reconciliation path. Current filled inventory alone therefore cannot enforce a hard aggregate cap; exposure handling must account for outstanding orders or cancel or block quotes as aggregate capacity is consumed. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[342-463] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[391-397] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[449-463] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[534-573] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[767-824] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[793-813] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
3. Maker fills are absent from the risk cap 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>reconcile records receipt-missing maker fills and adds them to per-market inv, but unlike
>record it neither calls addAssetExposure nor persists the corresponding exposure row. Because
>resting post-only fills are intentionally recovered from counterparties' transactions, subsequent
>cap decisions and the risk panel can omit the strategy's normal maker inventory.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[core/internal/maker/engine.go[R807-812]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/6/files#diff-5fa2c2f0354a49f1be3c74a5784df117c6be458f3be5b711bf5103878f93622fR807-R812) > >```diff >+ netAsset := e.addAssetExposure(in.Asset, signed) >+ >+ if e.Ledger != nil { >+ if err := e.Ledger.UpsertExposure(ctx, in.Asset, netAsset, e.Params.MaxAssetExposure); err != nil { >+ e.Log.Printf("ledger: record exposure %s: %v", in.Asset, err) >+ } >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Reconciled maker fills missing aggregate and persisted exposure breaks the new risk-control feature.
>
> > [PR-#2](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/2) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The receipt-processing path updates both aggregate asset state and the exposure table, while
>reconciliation is explicitly responsible for ingesting resting maker fills absent from the engine's
>own transaction receipts. After successfully recording such a fill, reconcile calls only
>addInventory, so assetInv—which feeds the exposure guard—and the persisted exposure used by the
>dashboard remain unchanged.
>
> > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[804-813]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L804-L813) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[911-919]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L911-L919) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[975-986]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L975-L986) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[840-852]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L840-L852) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[802-820]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L802-L820) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[943-990]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L943-L990) > [core/cmd/dashboard/main.go[464-476]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/cmd/dashboard/main.go/#L464-L476) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Update aggregate asset exposure when `reconcile` discovers a maker fill. Resolve the fill's asset, update `assetInv`, and persist the resulting total in the exposure ledger through the same transactionally safe path used for receipt-decoded fills. > >## Issue Context >Resting post-only maker fills normally occur in a counterparty's transaction and therefore lack the engine's submission receipt; they are intentionally recovered through `reconcile`. Its successful fill path currently records the fill and updates only per-market inventory, leaving both the aggregate used by subsequent cap decisions and the persisted exposure shown in the risk panel incomplete. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[793-824] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[911-990] >- core/internal/ledger/ledger.go[483-518] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

4. Restarted engines ignore open exposure 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>New initializes assetInv as an empty map, and neither startup nor reconciliation reconstructs
>per-asset exposure from persisted exposure or unsettled ledger fills before trading begins. After a
>restart, positions in still-live windows—including fills older than reconciliation’s 30-minute
>scan—are treated as flat by asset-cap decisions until new fills repopulate the map, allowing
>aggregate exposure to exceed the configured limit.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[core/internal/maker/engine.go[R98-101]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/6/files#diff-5fa2c2f0354a49f1be3c74a5784df117c6be458f3be5b711bf5103878f93622fR98-R101) > >```diff >+ intents: make(chan Intent, 256), >+ running: map[string]context.CancelFunc{}, >+ inv: map[string]float64{}, >+ assetInv: map[string]float64{}, >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Restart state failing to restore active exposure is a concrete reliability gap in the PR’s core
>feature.
>
> > [PR-#2](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/2) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The constructor creates an empty aggregate exposure map, while no startup path loads the ledger’s
>persisted exposure rows before spawning trading loops. Reconciliation runs later on a timer, scans
>only the previous 30 minutes even though a window can remain live for 240 minutes, treats
>ledger-known fills as already processed, and updates only per-market inventory, so it cannot
>reliably restore the per-asset state used by the cap.
>
> > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[95-102]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L95-L102) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[391-397]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L391-L397) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[943-952]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L943-L952) > [core/internal/ledger/ledger.go[483-518]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/ledger/ledger.go/#L483-L518) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[920-937]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L920-L937) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[975-990]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L975-L990) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Reconstruct in-memory per-market and per-asset exposure from authoritative ledger or indexer data before accepting new trading decisions after an engine restart, so unsettled positions are included in asset-cap enforcement. > >## Issue Context >The aggregate exposure map starts empty after every process restart even when unsettled positions exist. The shared ledger persists fills and exposes generic exposure rows, but the persisted `exposure` table is currently used for dashboard purposes and no startup path loads it into enforcement state. Reconciliation starts only after trading has begun, scans the prior 30 minutes despite live windows potentially containing positions up to 240 minutes old, skips fills already known to the ledger, and updates only per-market inventory rather than rebuilding per-asset aggregates. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[95-102] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[181-224] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[391-397] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[920-992] >- core/internal/ledger/ledger.go[483-518] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
5. Settled positions keep blocking new trades 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>addAssetExposure/record only adds receipt fills to assetInv, while reap deletes the
>corresponding per-market inventory and terminal settlement records the outcome without subtracting
>that market’s contribution or updating the ledger value. After completed windows accumulate enough
>same-direction fills, their expired positions remain counted indefinitely and later live windows on
>the same asset can be refused at a cap that no longer reflects current risk.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[core/internal/maker/engine.go[R807-812]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/6/files#diff-5fa2c2f0354a49f1be3c74a5784df117c6be458f3be5b711bf5103878f93622fR807-R812) > >```diff >+ netAsset := e.addAssetExposure(in.Asset, signed) >+ >+ if e.Ledger != nil { >+ if err := e.Ledger.UpsertExposure(ctx, in.Asset, netAsset, e.Params.MaxAssetExposure); err != nil { >+ e.Log.Printf("ledger: record exposure %s: %v", in.Asset, err) >+ } >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Never removing settled exposure causes persistent false cap refusals and stale risk telemetry.
>
> > [PR-#2](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/2) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Receipt fills increment assetInv, but window teardown only deletes e.inv[marketID], and
>settlement only records the outcome. Neither lifecycle path removes the settled market’s
>contribution from the aggregate or persists the reduced value to the ledger, even though the new
>state and ledger schema describe exposure across currently open windows.
>
> > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[804-813]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L804-L813) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[236-245]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L236-L245) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[870-907]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L870-L907) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[840-852]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L840-L852) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[236-246]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L236-L246) > [core/internal/maker/engine.go[802-813]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/maker/engine.go/#L802-L813) > [core/internal/ledger/ledger.go[83-94]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/ledger/ledger.go/#L83-L94) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description > >Make aggregate asset exposure represent positions across currently open windows rather than accumulating receipt fills indefinitely. Track each market’s contribution, remove it from the asset total when the market expires or reaches terminal settlement, and persist the resulting aggregate value to the ledger. > >## Issue Context > >Per-market quote inventory is deleted during reaping, but `assetInv` has no corresponding lifecycle update and currently stores no market-to-asset contribution that teardown can use. Settlement only records the outcome, leaving both the aggregate map and ledger row stale even though the feature and dashboard define exposure in terms of windows open right now. > >## Fix Focus Areas > >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[236-246] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[767-824] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[840-852] >- core/internal/maker/engine.go[865-908] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

6. Voids make model skill look better 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>RecentHealth assigns voids an outcome of 0.5, but health still applies a fixed Brier baseline
>loss of 0.25 for an always-0.5 predictor instead of the correct zero loss on those points.
>Whenever the rolling sample contains voids, their fraction changes the correct baseline while the
>fixed denominator artificially increases the reported skill percentage.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[core/cmd/dashboard/main.go[R453-457]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/6/files#diff-c987c996d7d4ff40b86bbdfe2507c39c9efef6a554253ff09d1b31cbbb42e7b8R453-R457) > >```diff >+ const baseline = 0.25 // Brier of "always predict 0.5", the same reference cmd/backtest scores against >+ brier, skill := 0.0, 0.0 >+ if n > 0 { >+ brier = sumSq / float64(n) >+ skill = 100 * (1 - brier/baseline) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Recent dashboard correctness findings were accepted; void-aware baseline is a clear metric bug.
>
> > [PR-#2](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/2) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The ledger emits Value: 0.5 for voided windows, consistent with existing attribution behavior that
>pays 0.5 per contract rather than producing a binary result, while the dashboard endpoint always
>uses a constant 0.25 baseline. Under the same squared-error formula used for the live forecast, an
>always-0.5 baseline has loss (0.5 - 0.5)^2 = 0 on each void, proving that the fixed baseline is
>inconsistent with the recorded targets.
>
> > [core/internal/ledger/ledger.go[559-573]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/ledger/ledger.go/#L559-L573) > [core/cmd/dashboard/main.go[447-460]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/cmd/dashboard/main.go/#L447-L460) > [core/internal/ledger/ledger.go[559-572]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/ledger/ledger.go/#L559-L572) > [core/internal/ledger/ledger.go[214-225]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/blob/fc7ab79bc4446f7b40f823b0d380dac1fe033988/core/internal/ledger/ledger.go/#L214-L225) >
>
>Agent prompt >

Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Compute health skill against a baseline consistent with the treatment of voided markets. Voided fills use a soft outcome of 0.5, while the dashboard currently retains the binary-outcome constant baseline loss of 0.25; either exclude voids from calibration scoring or calculate baseline loss per point from the recorded outcome. > >## Issue Context >For a point whose value is 0.5, an always-0.5 predictor has squared error zero, not 0.25. Because the current endpoint always uses the fixed 0.25 denominator, it overstates reported skill whenever the rolling sample contains voids, and changing the void fraction changes the correct aggregate baseline. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- core/internal/ledger/ledger.go[559-573] >- core/cmd/dashboard/main.go[447-460] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
7. Ledger failures look like no exposure 🐞 Bug ◔ Observability
>
>Description >
> >
>The system page discards every rejection from api.risk, leaving risk null and rendering the same
>message used when the exposure list is genuinely empty. A ledger read failure returned by
>/api/risk is therefore presented to operators as “No exposure recorded yet,” concealing loss of
>the new risk telemetry.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[web/src/app/system/page.tsx[25]](https://github.com/PrinceXDev/firstbid/pull/6/files#diff-2b012d91f7c24b4deacd78871a77ca3343b6a50285df7477a69d9637e8ea1069R25-R25) > >```diff >+ api.risk(ac.signal).then(setRisk).catch(() => {}); >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Suppressing API failures as empty state is a clear observability defect in the new risk panel.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The risk promise has an empty rejection handler, and the rendering branch treats both null and an
>empty response as no recorded exposure. The backend explicitly returns HTTP 500 for a failed ledger
>query, so this is a reachable operational failure rather than a hypothetical state.
>

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
